title: signbit reads the sign of -0.0 and of NaN
verdict: recorded: signbit is a black box Lean evaluates away from zero and NaN
description: `signbit(x)` is the IEEE sign bit of the double `x`: TRUE for `'-0.0'::DOUBLE`, `-(0.0::DOUBLE)` and `-'nan'::DOUBLE`, FALSE for `+0.0` and `'nan'::DOUBLE`. The literal `-0.0` is a DECIMAL, which converts to `+0.0`, so `signbit(-0.0)` is FALSE. An integer argument is converted to a double.
The docs are silent on the type of the literal `-0.0`, a DECIMAL that loses the sign: a docs gap. No upstream test pins `signbit(-0.0)` of the literal; it may change between versions.
reference: The model's double codes have one zero and one NaN (`core/Sverify/Core/Float.lean`), so they do not determine `signbit` there. `signbit` is a black box (#328) whose only law is `nonNull`; Lean's evaluator gives `c < 0` for every other code and refuses to print rows at zero and NaN.

evidence.sql: SELECT signbit(-0.0), signbit(0.0), signbit('nan'::DOUBLE), signbit(-1), signbit(NULL::DOUBLE), signbit(-'nan'::DOUBLE)
evidence.observed: false, false, false, true, NULL, true

evidence.note: signbit: FLOAT and DOUBLE overloads, std::signbit
signbit: 'Returns whether the signbit is set or not'
FLOAT and DOUBLE: signbit(-3) true, stored -0.0 true, signbit(abs(-0.0)) false
